description: Test fixture corpus for casr provider readers, writers, and round-trip tests.

cc_simple.intent: Basic 4-message conversation with all fields populated.

cc_complex.intent: Tool use/result content blocks, content arrays, file-history-snapshot skip.

cc_missing_workspace.intent: Session with no cwd field. Tests workspace=None path.

cc_unicode.intent: Japanese, Chinese, and emoji characters. Tests UTF-8 fidelity.

cc_malformed.intent: Malformed JSON lines interspersed with valid messages. Tests error tolerance.

codex_modern.intent: Modern JSONL envelope with session_meta, event_msg, response_item.

codex_legacy.intent: Legacy single-JSON format with session and items keys.

codex_token_count.intent: Includes token_count events that should be skipped as non-conversational.

codex_reasoning.intent: Agent reasoning events extracted as Assistant messages with author=reasoning.

codex_malformed.intent: Malformed lines interspersed with valid Codex entries. Tests error tolerance.

gmi_simple.intent: Basic Gemini session with user/model message types.

gmi_grounding.intent: Grounding metadata and citations in model responses. Tests extra field preservation.

gmi_missing_workspace.intent: No workspace inferrable from content. Tests workspace=None.

gmi_gemini_role.intent: Uses 'gemini' role type instead of 'model'. Tests normalize_role mapping.

gmi_jsonl_rewind.intent: Current Gemini JSONL: header, $set metadata updates, a message re-appended under an id already recorded, a $rewindTo that undoes two turns, and one record type this reader does not recognise. Proves the reader folds the log instead of concatenating it.

agy_simple.intent: Antigravity (agy) conversation. uuid==db filename stem; content read from sibling brain/<uuid>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl. Tests housekeeping-step drop, USER_REQUEST unwrap, tool-call extraction, model pin, and gmi disambiguation.

grok_simple.intent: Grok Build (grok CLI) session: ACP session-update stream in updates.jsonl + summary.json metadata under sessions/<percent-encoded-cwd>/<uuid>/. Envelope and user_message_chunk/hook_execution/retry_state shapes captured from a real grok 0.2.103 session (sanitized); assistant/tool shapes per the public ACP schema. Tests chunk coalescing, tool_call+tool_call_update merge, unknown-kind tolerance, and summary-driven title/model/workspace.

cline_simple.intent: Basic Cline task fixture with API conversation history and taskHistory metadata.

amp_simple.intent: Basic Amp centralized thread fixture with workspace and timestamp metadata.

aider_simple.intent: Basic Aider markdown history fixture with model/workspace metadata lines.

chatgpt_simple.intent: ChatGPT mapping-format conversation with parent chain. Float timestamps, model_slug metadata.

clawdbot_simple.intent: Real @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent SessionManager transcript — the envelope every published clawdbot writes (clawdbot depends on that package and drives the file via SessionManager.open/appendMessage). Header, message entries with text/thinking/toolCall blocks and a toolResult, plus a model_change.
clawdbot_simple.provenance: Generated by the published @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.32.3 SessionManager itself, driven exactly as clawdbot drives it (SessionManager.open on a not-yet-existing file, then the header stamp from dist/agents/pi-embedded-runner/session-manager-init.js). Only the wall clock was frozen, so the timestamps are stable; entry ids are the real randomUUID().slice(0,8) values. Not hand-written.

vibe_simple.intent: Basic Vibe JSONL conversation with role/content/timestamp fields.

factory_simple.intent: Factory JSONL with session_start header and typed message entries. Model from message.model.

openclaw_simple.intent: Real @openclaw/ai SessionManager transcript. Covers the record types that separate OpenClaw's fork from pi: session_info, an entry-level custom_message, a bashExecution message (no `content` field), thinking blocks carrying `.thinking`, a toolResult, a custom entry, and a branch_summary produced by an actual rewind — so the file contains an abandoned branch that a linear read would resurrect.
openclaw_simple.provenance: Generated by the published openclaw@2026.7.1-2 SessionManager itself (which vendors @openclaw/ai@2026.7.1-2, not @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent), driven through its own append API: appendMessage / appendCustomMessageEntry / appendCustomEntry / appendModelChange / appendThinkingLevelChange / appendSessionInfo / branchWithSummary. Only the wall clock was frozen, so entry timestamps are stable; entry ids are the real randomUUID().slice(0,8) values and the header id is a real uuidv7. Not hand-written. The previous fixture at this path was synthetic and encoded casr's expectations rather than OpenClaw's output: it stamped `version` as the string "0.1.0" where OpenClaw stamps the number 3, used sequential m1/m2 ids, and carried no `parentId` on any entry, so it could not express the tree the format is built on.

piagent_simple.intent: Pi-Agent JSONL with session header, toolResult role, and toolCall blocks. Underscore filename.

cur_simple.intent: Cursor state.vscdb SQLite with modern v0.40+ format. 4-message conversation with workspace in bubble.

opc_simple.intent: OpenCode SQLite with sessions+messages tables. 4-message session with model metadata.

edge_empty_content_cc.intent: Empty and whitespace-only content messages that should be skipped.

edge_null_timestamps_cc.intent: All messages lack timestamps. Tests None timestamp handling.

edge_long_message_cc.intent: Very long message body (900+ chars). Tests no-truncation preservation.

edge_single_sided_cc.intent: User-only messages, no assistant. Validation should flag as error.

kiro_ide_session.intent: Kiro IDE session in the bucketed store: metadata plus a twelve-line messages.jsonl covering session_start (the prompt that opened the session — a message, not a marker), a mid-turn user payload, assistant Reasoning, assistant Say, two tool_call/tool_result pairs (one failing), and the three lifecycle events (turn_start, usage_summary, turn_end) a reader must NOT count as messages.
kiro_ide_session.provenance: Not a capture — Kiro IDE needs a GUI and an AWS login, so no session could be recorded on this machine, and this is stated rather than dressed up. Every field is transcribed from the zod schemas recovered verbatim from the shipped Kiro IDE 1.0.212 linux-x64 build (kiro-ide-1.0.212-stable-linux-x64.tar.gz), file Kiro/resources/app/extensions/kiro.kiro-agent/dist/extension.js: `SessionMetadataSchema` and `PersistedMessageSchema = z.object({id: z.string(), timestamp: z.string(), payload: MessagePayloadSchema})`, whose 23-arm discriminated union names every `payload.type` used here. Each lifecycle payload now carries exactly its schema's required fields and invents none: `SessionStartPayloadSchema` requires `{agentType, content, forcedRole, messageId}` and has no `sessionId`; `TurnStartPayloadSchema` has only an optional `executionId` and no `turnId`; `TurnEndPayloadSchema` requires `stopReason: z.string().min(1)`; `UsageSummaryPayloadSchema` requires `promptTurnSummaries` and has neither `inputTokens` nor `outputTokens`. The earlier revision of this fixture had all four wrong, which nothing caught because they were the four records the reader discarded. The record id `session_start_<sessionId>` is the shipped `Y24(e17)`. The on-disk layout the test places these at (`<root>/sessions/<bucket>/<id>/{session.json,messages.jsonl}`) is from `SessionPersistence.getSessionPath`/`saveSession` in the same file, and the bucket name `b550143462be8201` was produced by running Kiro's own `workspace-hash-Dq3QXXpU.js` functions (copied out verbatim) under node against `["/home/u/demo-project"]`, not by re-implementing the hash; `printf '/home/u/demo-project' | sha256sum | cut -c1-16` agrees.

kiro_ide_session_global.intent: Kiro IDE session with `workspacePaths: []`. Kiro buckets these under the literal `_global`, and the bucket name is a sha256 prefix that names no path, so the session's workspace is genuinely unknowable and must read as None rather than as an inverted directory name.
kiro_ide_session_global.provenance: Same class and same source file as `kiro_ide_session`. The `_global` bucket literal is `a20 = "_global"` in workspace-hash-Dq3QXXpU.js, returned by `p27` when the path array is empty; confirmed by running that function under node.

cursor_agent_transcript.intent: cursor-agent CLI transcript (the store the Cursor state.vscdb reader never looked at): a metadata/overview line, user, assistant with a text block and a tool_use block, a tool-role line, and a turn_ended line. The metadata and turn_ended lines must not be counted as messages. The tool-role line is deliberately kept: it is not something the LOCAL writer can produce, but it is exactly what the cloud exporter writes to the same path, so a reader has to handle it — see provenance.
cursor_agent_transcript.provenance: Not a capture — cursor-agent refuses to run a turn without a Cursor account, so no real conversation could be recorded on this machine. The line shape is transcribed from the writer itself in the shipped cursor-agent 2026.07.23-e383d2b linux-x64 package (downloads.cursor.com/lab/2026.07.23-e383d2b/linux/x64/agent-cli-package.tar.gz), module `../agent-transcript/dist/index.js` in 7923.index.js: the emitter is `{role: t.role, message: {content: r}}` with `r` entries `{type:'text',text}` and `{type:'tool_use',name,input}`, plus the `{type:'metadata',metadata:{overview}}` prefix line and the `{type:'turn_ended',...}` suffix line. The path the test places it at (`<dataDir>/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl`) is `sk()` in `../agent-transcript/dist/paths.js` joined with `Xq()` from `../cursor-config/dist/index.js`; the slug `home-u-demo-project` was produced by running cursor-agent's own `r_` from `../utils/dist/workspace-paths.js` under node. An empirical run of the shipped binary under a sandboxed HOME created `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>` for its own cwd, confirming the root. THE FORMAT HAS TWO WRITERS, which is why line 4 looks unlike the rest. (1) The local writer is `I()` in 7923.index.js, described above; it composes content from text, thinking and toolCalls only and never emits the toolResult its own `M()` computes, so a locally-run session can contain no tool output and no role:'tool' line — `I()` returns undefined for a message that has only a toolResult, and `$()` drops it. (2) The cloud exporter is `handleCloudTranscript` in ./src/commands/cloud-transcript.ts (`cursor-agent cloud transcript <id>`, whose own --help says it 'writes to disk under ~/.cursor/projects'): 6363.index.js `f()` maps the backend's protobuf conversation through `p()`, which turns each tool row into `{role:'tool', content:[{type:'text', text: JSON.stringify({tool_call_id, tool_name, tool_args, tool_result}, void 0, 2)}]}`, then passes it through the SAME `$()`/`I()` serializer and writes it via `kw()` — i.e. to `<dataDir>/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl`, the identical path the local writer uses and the one this reader globs. Line 4 of this fixture is that shape, generated from `p()`'s own JSON.stringify. Line 3's text block carries only `text`: an earlier revision gave it `name:''` and `input:{}`, which no writer emits.

cursor_agent_chat_store.intent: cursor-agent CLI chat store — the half of the CLI's session that is NOT the transcript. Supplies the title, creation time and model the transcript does not carry, and, when no transcript exists for its id, is the unreadable candidate that must reach `list`'s `skipped` list instead of being dropped.
cursor_agent_chat_store.provenance: Built by sqlite3 from the DDL executed verbatim by cursor-agent 2026.07.23-e383d2b, `../cursor-sdk-local-runtime/dist/run-store/sqlite-blob-store.js` `initializeDriver`: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blobs (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data BLOB); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);` with `PRAGMA user_version = 1`. The `meta['0']` row is hex of UTF-8 JSON because that is what the shipped codec does — `L.serialize` is `TextEncoder.encode(JSON.stringify({...metadata, latestRootBlobId: hex}))` and it is stored through `nj = (e) => Buffer.from(e).toString('hex')` (`../agent-kv/dist/index.js`); its field names are the keys of that class's own zod schema. The `meta['0']` row deliberately carries a `blobEncryptionKey`: every real chat has one, because the shipped default-metadata factory ends `subagentInfo: void 0, blobEncryptionKey: Q()` and `Q()` is 32 bytes of `crypto.getRandomValues` hex-encoded, which `./src/utils/blob-encryption-key-header.ts` then sends to Cursor's backend as the `x-blob-encryption-key` header. The value here (`5eec6e7a…`) is synthetic, but it is shaped and positioned exactly like a real one — 64 lowercase hex, last key in the object — so that a reader which copies this object wholesale is caught. Omitting it is why the original wholesale-copy disclosure shipped unnoticed; tests/cursor_secret_test.rs now fails if it is removed. The `blobs` row is a stub: the real conversation is a blob graph this reader does not decode. Note that is a statement about this reader, not the format — the root blob is protobuf (`agent.v1.ConversationStateStructure`), but its field 1 `root_prompt_messages_json` is `repeated bytes` of blob ids whose blobs are plain JSON (`JSON.parse`), nothing is encrypted at rest (`setBlob` writes `Buffer.from(data)` straight in), and the CLI's own `generateTranscript` rebuilds a full transcript from one store.db alone.
cursor_agent_chat_store.no_expected_because: There is no canonical session to expect. This fixture's correct outcome is a read failure that reaches `list`'s `skipped` list, which is asserted in tests/second_store_test.rs (cursor_agent_chat_without_transcript_is_reported_not_dropped) rather than in an expected/ golden. The secret-redaction behaviour is asserted separately in tests/cursor_secret_test.rs.
